items.gloss: the highest good is like water
items.angle: Trace one idea or artifact across cultures, with attribution of traditions and no invented chronology.
items.topicConnection: Mandatory scope: connect this Chinese-origin term to Japanese Buddhism or compare its meaning with Buddhist practice; do NOT write a wholly unrelated Chinese history passage. Clearly distinguish traditions, never fabricate direct influence. A careful conceptual comparison is enough.

items.reading: じょうざぶぶっきょう
items.angle: Compare lived practice with an oversimplified popular description, without ending in the same moral.

items.gloss: Advaita Vedānta, the doctrine of non-dualism
items.angle: Explain how a primary text uses this term; omit attributed quotations unless exact and reliable.
items.factNote: Advaita Vedanta is not interchangeable with Buddhist no-self or classical Yoga dualism.

items.angle: A visit to a place prompts a compact interpretation of the term; imagined ordinary scenes must not be presented as reported events.
Discuss the difference between a doctrinal claim and observable experience, avoid formulaic warnings.
A concrete temple object or ordinary scene opens the passage; use it to explain the term through a distinct detail.
items.factNote: Zen emphasis on transmission beyond verbal formulation is not a ban on reading and writing.

items.angle: Start with a distinction that matters when reading a historical source; explain why this distinction changes interpretation.
A small dilemma in daily practice leads to a reflective argument; do not force a scientific analogy.
items.surfaceNote: The literal target must occur exactly once, including substrings inside longer compounds; avoid repeating that character sequence.

items.angle: A casual friend-to-friend explanation beginning mid-conversation; no canned ending and no repeated two-person Q/A frame.

note: All passages remain topic india, including comparative philosophy and meditation science. Tradition and legend must be marked as such. For the target バガヴァッド・ギーター only, mentioning that text is required despite the general avoid list. Avoid these automatic last-six-character endings: る必要がある,みてください,ほかならない,すくなります,かもしれない,見えてきます,ているのです. End with a specific detail or concrete consequence.
